title: Building durable Agents with Workflow DevKit & AI SDK - Peter Wielander, Vercel
talk_summary: Vercel engineer demonstrates converting an AI coding agent to Workflow DevKit by separating deterministic orchestration from retryable, cached steps, adding resumable streams, sleep/webhook suspension, and observability. The talk emphasizes durable execution for long-running agents and versioned upgrades, with most features shown via code and local/prod inspection UI.

takeaways.what_they_do: Mark LLM and tool calls as steps; cache each step's inputs/outputs so a failed or restarted workflow rehydrates state and resumes from the last completed step instead of replaying everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the step completes, we cach the output and say this step has been run um to completion

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the workflow/orchestration function deterministic and side-effect-free; put all side effects in isolated steps that can be retried and observed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the workflow orchestration layer needs to be deterministic. So it can be rerun um in a in a uh deterministic fashion

takeaways.technique: Durable sleep and webhook wait states
takeaways.what_they_do: Use sleep to suspend a workflow without consuming resources, and webhooks to suspend until a human or external system calls a URL; then resume exactly where it paused.
takeaways.evidence_quote: await web hook and this will suspend for as long as necessary to uh someone to click on this URL

takeaways.what_they_do: Decouple the stream from the API handler by associating it with a workflow/run ID; clients reconnect to a stream endpoint and resume from a start index.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the stream is not bound to the API handler. This means that at any point we can resume this stream

takeaways.what_they_do: Every marked step emits a span with inputs, outputs, and associated events; the same inspection UI works locally and in production, with OpenTelemetry export planned.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every step everything that is marked as a step will have a uh span here and you can inspect the inputs the outputs

takeaways.what_they_do: Each deployment/version has step signatures; a run knows its version, and upgrades are allowed only after checking compatibility with existing step/event signatures, otherwise cancel and rerun.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can call run.upgrade upgrade to see if it's compatible with a new version to upgrade it to that version
